    #Question 2

    #Part (a)

    Assume a steady flow process with no change in mass of the system. Assume both
    the turbine and heat exchanger are adiabatic — no heat loss to surroundings.

    From Table A5, at P1​=20 MPa,

    Tsat@20000​=365.75°C

    Since T1​>Tsat@20000​, initial state is superheated vapor.

    From Table A5, at P2​=5 MPa,

    Tsat@5000​=263.94°C

    Since T2​>Tsat@5000​, state 2 is superheated vapor.

    From Table A6, at P1​=20 MPa and T1​=500°C,

    h1​=3241.2 kJ/kg

    From Table A6, at P2​=5 MPa and T2​=300°C,

    h2​=2925.7 kJ/kg

    From Table A5, at P3​=100 kPa,

    h3​=2675.0 kJ/kg

    Q˙​−W˙=m˙Δh

    W˙=−m˙(31​h2​+32​h3​−h1​)

    W˙=−2[31​(2925.7)+32​(2675.0)−3241.2]

    W˙=965.27 kW

    #Part (b)

    From Table A5, at P4​=1000 kPa,

    h4​=762.51 kJ/kg

    Q˙​−W˙=31​m˙Δh

    Q˙​=31​m˙(h4​−h2​)

    Q˙​=31​(2)(762.51−2925.7)

    Q˙​=−1442.13 kJ/s

    Negative sign indicates heat loss from the steam into the feed water.

    #Part (c)

    hi​=4.18(30+273)=1266.54 kJ/kg

    Q˙​−W˙=m˙Δh

    Q˙​=m˙(he​−hi​)

    1442.13=10(he​−1266.54)

    Heat loss from turbine steam is heat gain by feed water.

    he​=1410.75 kJ/kg

    Te​=4.181410.75​=337.5 K=64.5°C

    P=100 kPa and T=99.61°C

    100−7580.96−75​=99.61−91.76T1′​−91.76​

    #Part (c)

    When piston starts leaving the spring, the spring is at it’s natural length.
    The spring is not exerting pressure on the piston. Thus, P2​=Patm​=100 kPa.

    From Table A5, at P2​=100 kPa,

    v2​=200.05(0.5)​=0.00125 m3/kg

    vf​=0.001043 m3kg

    vg​=1.6941 m3kg

    #Part (d)

    State 1: P1​=50 kPa, T1​=50°C, v1​=0.001012 m3/kg

    State 1’: P1′​=80.96 kPa, T1′​=93.631°C, v1′​=0.001012 m3/kg

    State 2: P2​=100 kPa, T2​=99.61°C, v2​=0.00125 m3/kg

    State 3: P3​=100 kPa, T3​=150°C, v3​= ?

    From state 1 to 1’, it is an isochoric process since piston only just starts moving at 1’.

    From state 1’ to 2, piston moves up and volume increases, thus there is work done.

    From state 2 to 3, it is an isobaric process since the spring is no longer in contact.

    From Table A5, at P3​=100 kPa, Tsat@100​=99.61°C.

    Since T3​>Tsat@100​, it is superheated vapor.

    From Table A6, at P3​=100 kPa and T3​=150°C,

    v3​=1.9367 m3/kg

    Vˉ1​=0.001012(20)=0.02024 m3

    Vˉ2​=0.00125(20)=0.025 m3

    Vˉ3​=1.9367(20)=38.734 m3

    Work done is total area under P-Vˉ graph.

    W=21​(80.96+100)(0.025−0.02024)+100(38.734−0.025)

    W=3871.3 J

    #Part (e)

    From Table A4, at T1​=50°C,

    u1​=uf​=209.33 kJ/kg

    From Table A6, at T3​=150°C,

    u3​=2582.9 kJ/kg

    m(u3​−u1​)=Q−W

    Q=20(2582.9−209.33)+3871.3

    Q=51.343 kJ

    #Part (c)

    #Part (i)

    Based on observation, point D will have the maximum gauge pressure.
    Since it is the furthest away from the axis of rotation, it will experience the
    greatest centrifugal force. Additionally, it is at the lowest point of the tank.

    dp=ρrω2 dr−ρ(g+az​) dz

    ∫AD​dp=∫AD​ ρrω2 dr−∫AD​ ρg dz

    PD​−PA​=ρω2[2r2​]AD​−ρg[z]AD​

    PD​−PA​=21​ρω2(4L2−L2)−ρg[0−(H+W)]

    PD​−PA​=23​ρω2L2+ρg(H+W)

    PD​=23​ρω2L2+ρg(H+W)

    Since A is exposed to atmosphere, gauge pressure PA​=0.

    #Part (ii)

    dp=ρrω2 dr−ρ(g+az​) dz

    ∫AC​dp=∫AC​ ρrω2 dr−∫AC​ ρg dz

    PC​=ρω2[2r2​]AC​−ρg[z]AC​

    PC​=−ρg[H−(H+W)]

    PC​=ρgW

    PD​=2PC​

    23​ρω2L2+ρg(H+W)=2ρgW

    23​ρω2L2=ρg(W−H)

    ω=3L22g(W−H)​​

    #Question 4

    #Part (a)

    P0​+21​ρV0​2+ρgz0​=P1​+21​ρV1​2+ρgz1​

    ρg(H+h1​)=21​ρV1​2

    V1​=2g(H+h1​)​

    P0​+21​ρV0​2+ρgz0​=P2​+21​ρV2​2+ρgz2​

    ρg(H+h2​)=21​ρV2​2

    V2​=2g(H+h2​)​

    For system to be in a steady state, Qin​=Qout​.

    Qin​=A1​V1​+A2​V2​

    Qin​=41​πD1​22g(H+h1​)​+41​π(D2​)22g(H+h2​)​

    Qin​=41​π[D1​22g(H+h1​)​+D2​22g(H+h2​)​]

    #Part (b)

    Qin(new)​=81​π[D1​22g(H+h1​)​+D2​22g(H+h2​)​]

    Qout​=Qin(old)​=41​π[D1​22g(H+h1​)​+D2​22g(H+h2​)​]

    dtdmsys​​=∂t∂​∫CV​ ρ dVˉ+∫CS​ ρV⋅n dA

    0=∂t∂​∫CV​ dVˉ−∫in​ V dA+∫out​ V dA

    0=∂t∂Vˉ​−Qin​+Qout​

    ∂t∂Vˉ​=Qin​−Qout​

    ∂t∂​ 41​πL2H=Qin​−Qout​

    41​πL2 ∂t∂H​=Qin​−Qout​

    ∫H0.5H​ 41​πL2 dH=∫0t​ Qin​−Qout​ dt

    t=∫H0.5H​ 4(Qin​−Qout​)πL2​ dH

    #EST S1 (2022 - 2023)

    #Question 1

    #Part (a)

    State 1: P1​=1000 kPa, T1​=400°C, V1​=0.2 m3

    State 2: P2​= ?, T2​= ?, V2​=0.19 m3

    Since piston is allowed to move freely, it is an isobaric process.
    However, due to the spring, pressure is not constant.

    P2​=P1​−Pspring​

    P2​=1000−0.05100(0.2)​

    P2​=600 kPa

    From Table A5, at P1​=1000 kPa, Tsat​=179.88°C.

    Since T1​=400°C>Tsat​, it is superheated steam.

    From Table A6, at P1​=1 MPa and T1​=400°C,

    v1​=0.30661 m3/kg

    m=0.306610.2​=0.65229 kg

    v2​=0.652290.19​=0.29128 m3/kg

    From Table A5, at P2​=600 kPa,

    vf​=0.001101 m3/kg

    vg​=0.31560 m3/kg

    Since vf​<v2​<vg​, it is liquid-vapor mixture.

    T2​=Tsat@600kPa​=158.83°C

    #Part (b)

    From Table A5, at P2​=600 kPa,

    vf​=0.001101 m3/kg

    vg​=0.31560 m3/kg

    v2​=0.29128 m3/kg

    v2​=vf​+xvfg​

    0.29128=0.001101+x(0.31560−0.001101)

    x=0.92267=92.267%

    mg​=0.92267(0.65229)=0.60185 kg

    mf​=0.65229−0.60185=0.050442 kg

    #Part (c)

    W=21​(600+1000)(0.19−0.2)=−8 kJ

    #Part (d)

    State 1: P1​=1000 kPa, T1​=400°C, V1​=0.2 m3

    State 2: P2​=600 kPa, T2​=158.83°C, V2​=0.19 m3

    State 3: P3​=300 kPa, T3​= ?, V3​=0.19 m3

    Since piston is not allowed to move, it is an isochoric process.

    v3​=v2​=0.29128 m3/kg

    From Table A5, at P3​=300 kPa,

    vf​=0.001073 m3/kg

    vg​=0.60582 m3/kg

    Since vf​<v3​<vg​, it is liquid-vapor mixture.

    0.29128=0.001073+x(0.60582−0.001073)

    x=0.47988

    From Table A5, at P3​=300 kPa,

    uf​=561.11 kJ/kg

    ufg​=1982.1 kJ/kg

    u3​=561.11+0.47988(1982.1)

    u3​=1512.28 kJ/kg

    From Table A6, at P1​=1 MPa and T1​=400°C,

    u1​=2957.9 kJ/kg

    Q−W=ΔU

    Q=m(u3​−u1​)+W

    Q=0.65229(1512.28−2967.9)+(−8)

    Q=−957.49 kJ

    #Part (e)

    #Question 2

    #Part (a)

    State 1: P1​=1 MPa, T1​=200°C

    State 2: P2​=1 MPa, T2​=179.88°C

    From Table A6, at P1​=1 MPa and T1​=200°C,

    v1​=0.20602 m3/kg

    h1​=2828.3 kJ/kg

    From Table A5, at P2​=1 MPa,

    v2​=vf​=0.001127 m3/kg

    h2​=hf​=762.51 kJ/kg

    Q˙​in​+W˙in​+m˙i​hi​=Q˙​out​+W˙out​+m˙e​he​

    (Q˙​in​−Q˙​out​)−(W˙out​−W˙in​)=m˙(he​−hi​)

    Q˙​−W˙=m˙(he​−hi​)

    Since no work is done by the steam,

    Q˙​=m˙(h2​−h1​)

    Q˙​=0.1(762.51−2828.3)

    Q˙​=−206.58 kJ/s

    #Part (b)

    State 2: P2​=1 MPa, T2​=179.88°C

    State 3: P3​=200 kPa, T3​= ?

    Since no heat is lost (adiabatic) and no work is done by the valve,

    h3​=h2​=762.51 kJ/kg

    From Table A5, at P3​=200 kPa,

    hg​=2706.3 kJ/kg

    #Part (c)

    State 4: P4​=100 kPa, T4​=25°C

    State 5: P5​=100 kPa, T5​= ?

    Since no heat is lost and no work is done by the condenser,

    m˙i​hi​=m˙e​he​

    m˙steam​(h1​−h2​)=m˙air​(h5​−h4​)

    m˙steam​(h1​−h2​)=m˙air​cp​(T5​−T4​)

    P4​V˙=m˙Rs​T4​

    m˙air​=0.287(25+273)100(4)​

    0.1(2828.3−762.51)=4.6769(1.005)(T5​−25)

    #Question 3

    #Part (a)

    Horizontal Force

    Since PB​ and PC​ are equal on both sides of the gate,
    only the slanted section of the gate experiences a net Fh​.

    Fh1​=21​ρgh1​A

    Fh1​=21​(1000)(9.81)(2)(2×1)

    Fh1​=19620 N (to the right)

    Fh2​=2ρgcos45°A

    Fh2​=2(1000)(9.81)cos45°(2×1)

    Fh2​=27747 N (to the left)

    Fh​=19620−27747=−8126.9 N (to the left)

    Taking moments about B,

    Fh​yh​=Fh1​yh1​+Fh2​yh2​

    −8126.9yh​=19620⋅31​(2)−27747⋅21​(2)

    yh​=1.8048 m

    Vertical Force

    Vertical force due to pressure of the water on both sides cancel each other out.

    There is only vertical force due to pressure of the compressed air.

    Fv​=2ρgcos45°A

    Fv​=2(1000)(9.81)cos45°(2)

    Fv​=27747 N (acting downwards)

    xv​=21​(2)=1 m
